findings.problem: The arrows in the DFT table turn the OPPOSITE way to the spinning arrow of scene 4. Scene 4 turns clockwise (sample 1 of the 1-spin test points down-right, then down, down-left, left, up-left, up, up-right). Row 1 of the table reads right, UP-right, up, up-left, left, down-left, down, DOWN-right, i.e. counter-clockwise, so rows 1 and 7 (and 2 and 6, 3 and 5) are mirrored. The scene-5 spec says each cell holds 'the test arrow for that sample', and the contract in common-4.js line 7 says it is 'exactly the angle A9.chain(k) uses', but the grid draws in raw SVG coordinates (y points down) with a = -TAU * ang / n (line 155), which is counter-clockwise on screen, whereas the wheel goes through the plot (y up) and is clockwise. The bars are unaffected (lengths are equal), but the table is the visual claim 'this is the same test as scene 4, for every speed'.
findings.fix: In A9.dftGrid use a screen angle of +TAU * W8.ang(r, c) / n (positive is clockwise in SVG), so row 1 reads right, down-right, down, down-left, left, up-left, up, up-right and row 7 the reverse. Add a build-time assert that cell (1, 1) points down-right and that every cell (k, n) has the same direction as A9.chain(k).arrows[n] with the sample scaling removed (x_n and y flipped for screen), so the two scenes cannot drift apart again.
findings.evidence: s4@3.5 (wheel arrow at sample 1 points down-right) against s5@6.8 and s5@3.0 (row 1, column 1 points up-right; row 2 reads right, up, left, down); node check: for k = 1, n = 1 the clockwise vector is (0.71, -0.71) in y-up coordinates, i.e. down-right on screen.

findings.problem: '18 minutes' and '0.02 seconds' (and the caption 'A million samples: 18 minutes or 0.02 seconds') only hold at an assumed speed of a billion multiplications a second (lesson 9.2's table: 'time at 1 billion per second'). The speed appears nowhere on screen, so the two times look like measured facts about the algorithms; a learner cannot check 1.1 x 10^12 products against 18 minutes, or ask what happens on a faster computer.
findings.fix: Show the assumption in the payoff: a grey tag right of 'direct DFT', for example 'at a billion products a second' (about 29 characters, about 460 px wide at 28 px, x 300 to 760, ends well inside x 924), popping with the red bar (10.8 to 11.2). Add an assert that COST.directMin uses 1e9 so the tag text and the number cannot disagree.
findings.evidence: s10@12.0, s10@13.0, s10@15.2 (no speed anywhere); grep for 'billion' in scene-10-halve.js and scene-11-recap.js finds nothing; lesson js/content/algo/algo-p9-x-05.js step 'The bill: N x N'.

findings.problem: The last caption 'Only odd waves are needed.' (and the tag 'odd waves only') is stated as a general rule, directly under the headline 'Add sine waves, get any shape'. It is only true for the square wave. Lesson 9.1 teaches the opposite for other shapes: a saw tooth needs every whole frequency (1, 1/2, 1/3, ...) and a triangle uses odd ones with weights 1, 1/9, 1/25. A first-time learner can leave thinking odd waves are enough for any shape.
findings.fix: Make the claim about the shape: caption 'A square wave needs only odd waves.' (7 words in 1.8 s, still under 4.5 words a second) and keep the tag 'odd waves only' (or 'square: odd waves only', 245 px wide is the limit).
findings.evidence: s3@11.0 (caption 'Only odd waves are needed.' under 'get any shape'); lesson js/content/algo/algo-p9-x-01.js, a9-series render(): amp() for kind 'saw' uses every j, for 'tri' 1/(2j-1)^2.

findings.problem: Row 3 says 'The FFT halves the work again and again'. What halves is the PROBLEM (8 samples, then 4, then 2, then 1); the work in the video goes 64 products, then 32 + 4 butterflies (scene 9), then 12 butterflies (scene 10), which is not 'halved again and again' and is not what the pictogram beside it shows (64 against 12). The recap is the takeaway the learner keeps, so it should be literally true.
findings.fix: Relabel to 'The FFT keeps halving\nthe problem' (21 and 11 characters, within the 22 per line rule), or 'The FFT shares the work\nby halving' (23 characters is too long, so prefer the first).
findings.evidence: s11@4.5 and s11@8.8 (row 3 label against the 64 products / 12 butterflies bars); scene-09-split.js tags 'was 64 products' and '32 + 4 butterflies'.

findings.problem: The caption 'The hum is one pair of bars' and the ticks 15 / 113 and 3 / 125 rest on the rule 'the partner of bar k is N minus k, with N = 128', but 128 is never shown (the only labels are 'bar number', 3, 15, 113, 125 and the tags 'with a hum', 'the hum', 'DFT', 'inverse DFT'). A first-time learner sees 113 appear from nowhere and cannot tell why the partner of 15 is 113 or why 3 pairs with 125, so 'both bars' looks arbitrary.
findings.fix: Put the number on screen: change the axis label to 'bar number (128 in all)', or add a small grey tag under the arch such as '15 + 113 = 128' (arch tag zone, 28 px, about 250 px wide), appearing with the arch (4.2 to 4.9). Keep it grey so it does not compete with the red 'the hum'.
findings.evidence: s8@5.5 and s8@7.2 (ticks 113 and 125, no 128 anywhere); grep '128' in scene-08-edit.js finds it only in comments; lesson js/content/algo/algo-p9-x-07.js step 'Remove a component: the notch' states 'N = 128 ... delete bins 15 and 113'.

findings.problem: Caption 'Right speed: the arrows line up and add.' (6.8 to 8.7) sits over a blue chain that zig-zags: the arrows alternate down-right and up-right, and samples 2 and 6 have no arrow at all (value 0). They do not literally line up; what is true is that every arrow leans right (cos squared is never negative) while the up and down parts cancel in pairs, so the total is long and horizontal. A careful learner may think the picture contradicts the caption.
findings.fix: Say what the picture shows: 'Right speed: they all lean right and add.' (8 words in 1.9 s, 4.2 a second). Optionally let the stat tag read 'total 4'.
findings.evidence: s4@7.9 (zig-zag chain under the orange total arrow); node check: x_n * (cos, -sin) at k = 1 has real part cos^2(2 PI n / 8) >= 0 for all n and imaginary parts +-0.5 that cancel.

findings.problem: Caption 5 '32 products and 4 butterflies, not 64.' (and the tag '32 + 4 butterflies') mixes units: caption 4 has just said a butterfly costs one product, so the true count is 32 + 4 = 36 products, and scene 10 then compares '12 butterflies' with '64 products' as if a butterfly were one product. All three statements are true, but a learner who adds them up gets 36 here and 12 there with no bridge.
findings.fix: Keep the picture; change caption 5 to '32 products plus 4 butterflies: about half of 64.' (or tag '32 + 4 = 36 products'), so the unit is the same as in scenes 5 and 10.
findings.evidence: s9@7.2 (caption 'One butterfly: one product, two answers.'), s9@11.5 (tag '32 + 4 butterflies' beside 'was 64 products'), s10@9.0 (12 butterflies against 'direct: 64 products').

findings.problem: Caption 4 'Go back: the hum is gone.' starts at 8.4, but the hum only finishes draining at 9.4 (g runs 8.2 to 9.4 and the wave turns green at 9.3 to 9.7). For about a second the caption states a result that the picture has not reached yet (s8@9.0 still shows a half-humming wave).
findings.fix: Start the caption at 9.0 (ends 10.6 is fine, 1.6 s for 6 words) or word it as the action: 'Go back: the hum drains away.' until 9.4.
findings.evidence: s8@9.0 (caption already reads 'the hum is gone', wave still ripples), s8@10.2 (clean green wave).

findings.problem: After the Hann window the two orange bars drop from 0.62 / 0.65 to 0.42, which can read as 'the window made the signal weaker' next to a caption about the leak shrinking. The fall is the window's own dimming (the Hann window averages 0.5) and the wider main peak (bars 7 and 10 at 0.09), not lost information; lesson 9.4 states the trade as 'lower skirts but a wider main peak'. Nothing is wrong, but the trade-off is not visible as a trade-off.
findings.fix: Optional: add the lesson's wording to the last caption, 'A window fades the ends: the leak shrinks, the peak widens.' (9 words needs 2.0 s; the caption is 2.1 s long, so check the 4.5 words a second limit), or leave as is.

findings.problem: 'Any signal is a sum of sine waves' (recap row 1) and 'How every signal splits into waves' (title sub line) are slightly stronger than the lessons: lesson 9.1 says 'any PERIODIC function' / 'a repeating signal', and scene 7 of this very video teaches that the DFT treats its window as repeating for ever.
findings.fix: Recap row 1: 'Any repeating signal\nis a sum of sine waves' (20 and 22 characters, within the limit). The title sub line is a storyboard-fixed tagline; leave it or use 'How a signal splits into waves'.
findings.evidence: s11@8.8 (row 1), s1@3.5 (sub line); lesson js/content/algo/algo-p9-x-01.js step 'Fourier's crazy idea (1807)' and takeaways.

findings.problem: Differences to keep in mind when the storyboard is used as the reference: (1) scene 8 uses a hum of strength 0.4 and no noise, while lesson 9.5's playground uses strength 0.6 plus noise (new example numbers are allowed, but the workshop and the lesson will show different heights); the storyboard also says 'the noisy blue wave', and the video draws none. (2) The storyboard says the measured aliased bar in scene 6 has height 0.9; the implementation draws 1.0, which is the real 8-sample DFT value (2 |X[1]| / 8 = 1), so the video is right and the storyboard wrong. (3) Scene 5's tag reads 'row number = spins' where the storyboard says 'row k tests k spins' (fine). No other storyboard number or string disagrees with the lessons: 5 Hz / 1 and 12 Hz / 0.5, N = 8 cosine and bars [0, 4, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 4], 7 Hz at 8 samples a second folds to 1 Hz and limit 4 Hz, 16 samples a second limit 8 Hz, N = 64 with 8 and 8.5 cycles (0.622 / 0.651 / skirt 0.037, 0.077, 0.105; Hann 0.42 and 0.09), N = 128 with bars 3 / 15 / 113 / 125 (64 / 25.6), 8 and 12 butterflies, 64 and 16 and 32 products, 1,048,576 samples (18.3 minutes, 0.021 s, ratio 52,429), all re-run with node and correct.
findings.fix: No video change needed. Optionally correct the storyboard JSON (scene 6 MEASURED 0.9 to 1.0) and, if wanted, use strength 0.6 in scene 8 to match lesson 9.5 exactly.
findings.evidence: videos/_plan/algo-9.json scene 6 spec ('v 0.9') against scene-06-alias.js line 29 (MEASURED = S8[A.fold], asserted 1) and s6@9.0; lesson js/content/algo/algo-p9-x-07.js (0.6 * sin hum, noiseAmp 0.3).
